description: ## Goal Implement Filament.Hooks.use_effect/2. Schedules side effects to run AFTER the render pass completes (not during render). The effect function may return a cleanup function that runs before the effect re-fires (when deps change) or on fiber unmount. Depends on: C1 (slot infrastructure + after_render hook in LiveView) and C2 (required for realistic tests that verify effects by inspecting state changes). Can run in parallel with C3 if needed, but tests are easier to write after C2 is merged. ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run 'bw comment flm-oue.4 "..."' describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. --- ## Effect lifecycle (read carefully before implementing) DURING RENDER: use_effect registers the effect — it does NOT run it immediately. The hook checks whether deps changed since last render: - If deps changed (or first render): add {slot_index, fiber_id, effect_fn, deps} to context.pending_effects - If deps unchanged: do nothing (effect is a no-op this render) It always reads and re-commits the slot, so the deps are preserved. AFTER RENDER: Filament.LiveView.run_pending_effects/1 (wired in C1) runs each pending effect: 1. If the slot has a cleanup fn stored from the PREVIOUS run: call the cleanup fn first 2. Call effect_fn.() — this runs the side effect 3. effect_fn.() returns either nil or a zero-arity cleanup fn 4. The cleanup fn (or nil) is stored back into the fiber's hook_slots for this slot ON UNMOUNT: Filament.Reconciler.unmount/1 currently just sets status to :unmounting. C4 extends unmount/1 to run cleanup functions for all fibers. See "Extend Filament.Reconciler.unmount/1" section below. --- ## 1. Add use_effect/2 to Filament.Hooks FILE: lib/filament/hooks.ex @doc """ Schedules a side effect to run after the render completes. effect_fn is called after the component renders. It may return a cleanup function (zero-arity fn returning :ok or any term) that is called: - Before the next time the effect runs (when deps change), OR - When the fiber unmounts If effect_fn returns nil (or :ok, which is ignored), no cleanup is stored. deps controls when the effect re-runs: - [] — run once on mount, cleanup on unmount - [dep1, dep2] — run when any dep changes (Kernel.== comparison), cleanup before re-run - :always — run on every render Example: use_effect(fn -> :timer.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) fn -> :ok end # cleanup: no cancel needed for one-shot timer end, []) Rules: call only at the top level of render/1. """ @spec use_effect((-> (-> term()) | nil), deps :: [term()] | :always) :: :ok def use_effect(effect_fn, deps) when is_function(effect_fn, 0) do {index, previous, ctx} = use_slot(:__unset__) # Determine whether deps changed. # previous slot value: :__unset__ | {prev_deps, cleanup_fn | nil} deps_changed? = case previous do :__unset__ -> true # first render — always run {_prev_deps, _} when deps == :always -> true {prev_deps, _} -> prev_deps != deps _ -> true # unexpected format — rerun to be safe end if deps_changed? do # Before registering the new effect, extract the old cleanup fn so # run_pending_effects can call it before running the new effect. old_cleanup = case previous do {_prev_deps, cleanup} when is_function(cleanup, 0) -> cleanup _ -> nil end # Register the effect in pending_effects. # Store {slot_index, fiber_id, effect_fn, deps, old_cleanup} so # run_pending_effects has everything it needs. effect_entry = {index, ctx.fiber_id, effect_fn, deps, old_cleanup} ctx = Process.get(:filament_render_context) Process.put(:filament_render_context, %{ctx | pending_effects: [effect_entry | ctx.pending_effects]}) end # Always commit the current slot so the previous cleanup fn is preserved # for the case where deps did NOT change (old_cleanup should not be lost). current_cleanup = case previous do {_prev_deps, cleanup} -> cleanup _ -> nil end commit_slot(index, {deps, current_cleanup}) :ok end --- ## 2. Update Filament.LiveView.run_pending_effects/1 FILE: lib/filament/live_view.ex C1 created run_pending_effects/1 with a placeholder structure. Update it to handle the new 5-tuple format {slot_index, fiber_id, effect_fn, deps, old_cleanup}: def run_pending_effects(socket) do effects = Map.get(socket.assigns, :_filament_pending_effects, []) if effects == [] do socket else tree = socket.assigns._filament_tree new_tree = Enum.reduce(effects, tree, fn {slot_index, fiber_id, effect_fn, deps, old_cleanup}, acc_tree -> # 1. Run old cleanup if present if is_function(old_cleanup, 0), do: old_cleanup.() # 2. Run the new effect new_cleanup = effect_fn.() new_cleanup = if is_function(new_cleanup, 0), do: new_cleanup, else: nil # 3. Store {deps, new_cleanup} in the fiber's hook_slots fiber = acc_tree[fiber_id] if fiber do new_slots = Map.put(fiber.hook_slots, slot_index, {deps, new_cleanup}) Map.put(acc_tree, fiber_id, %{fiber | hook_slots: new_slots}) else acc_tree # fiber was unmounted between render and after_render end end) assign(socket, _filament_tree: new_tree, _filament_pending_effects: []) end end --- ## 3. Extend Filament.Reconciler.unmount/1 to run cleanups FILE: lib/filament/reconciler.ex Currently unmount/1 sets status to :unmounting and returns :ok. Extend it to extract and run cleanup functions from all fibers' hook_slots: def unmount(tree) do Enum.each(tree, fn {_fiber_id, fiber} -> Enum.each(fiber.hook_slots, fn {_index, {_deps, cleanup}} when is_function(cleanup, 0) -> cleanup.() _ -> :ok end) end) :ok end The order of cleanup execution is not guaranteed (map iteration order). If order matters for application logic, that is the application's responsibility. --- ## Test fixtures Create test/support/fixtures/timer_component.ex — a component that uses use_effect to track mount/unmount via a test-observable side channel (Agent): defmodule Filament.Test.Fixtures.TimerComponent do use Filament.Component defcomponent __MODULE__ do prop :tracker, :any, required: true # an Agent pid for test observation def render(%{tracker: tracker}) do {count, _set_count} = use_state(0) use_effect(fn -> Agent.update(tracker, fn state -> Map.update(state, :mounted, 1, &(&1 + 1)) end) fn -> Agent.update(tracker, fn state -> Map.update(state, :cleaned_up, 1, &(&1 + 1)) end) end end, []) # run once on mount ~F""" {count} """ end end end --- ## Tests Create test/filament/use_effect_test.exs. All rung-1 tests use the with_render_ctx helper and a mock LiveView socket (or simulate the pending_effects flow manually — see below). For testing without a full LiveView, use this helper to simulate the after-render step: defp flush_effects(socket_assigns, fiber_tree) do # Build a minimal socket-like map and call run_pending_effects directly. # This is only for unit testing. In production, LiveView calls it via attach_hook. fake_socket = %{assigns: Map.merge(socket_assigns, %{_filament_tree: fiber_tree})} Filament.LiveView.run_pending_effects(fake_socket) end # Note: run_pending_effects uses Phoenix.LiveView.assign/2. For unit tests, either # mock it or start a test LiveView. Prefer the rung-4 test approach for integration. # Simpler alternative: extract the effect-running logic into a pure function # Filament.LiveView.apply_effects(pending_effects, fiber_tree) :: {new_tree, ran_count} # that does NOT call assign/2, and test that directly. # THEN run_pending_effects calls apply_effects and wraps in assign. # This refactor makes effects fully unit-testable. Implement it this way. Add to lib/filament/live_view.ex: @doc false # internal, exposed for testing def apply_effects(pending_effects, fiber_tree) do Enum.reduce(pending_effects, {fiber_tree, 0}, fn {slot_index, fiber_id, effect_fn, deps, old_cleanup}, {acc_tree, count} -> if is_function(old_cleanup, 0), do: old_cleanup.() new_cleanup = effect_fn.() new_cleanup = if is_function(new_cleanup, 0), do: new_cleanup, else: nil fiber = acc_tree[fiber_id] new_tree = if fiber do new_slots = Map.put(fiber.hook_slots, slot_index, {deps, new_cleanup}) Map.put(acc_tree, fiber_id, %{fiber | hook_slots: new_slots}) else acc_tree end {new_tree, count + 1} end) end Update run_pending_effects/1 to delegate to apply_effects/2. ### Tests 1. Effect runs on first render (deps = []) - Render TimerComponent via Reconciler.mount/3 with a test Agent - Simulate after-render by calling apply_effects with the pending_effects from mount - Assert Agent state shows mounted: 1 2. Effect does NOT re-run on second render when deps unchanged (deps = []) - Call mount then update (with same props) then apply_effects again - Assert Agent state shows mounted: 1 (still, not 2) 3. Effect re-runs when deps change - Create a component with use_effect(fn, [dep_value]) - First render with dep_value = :a — effect runs - Second render with dep_value = :b — effect runs again - Assert fun called twice 4. Cleanup runs before effect re-fires - Three renders with changing deps - Assert cleanup called once before second run, twice total before third run 5. Cleanup runs on unmount (via Reconciler.unmount/1) - Mount TimerComponent, apply effects (mounted: 1) - Call Reconciler.unmount(tree) - Assert Agent state shows cleaned_up: 1 6. deps == :always causes effect to run on every render - Three renders, assert effect called three times 7. Effect fn that returns nil — no crash, no cleanup stored - use_effect(fn -> nil end, []) - apply_effects — runs without error - Unmount — no crash (no cleanup to call) 8. Stale fiber (fiber_id not in tree) — apply_effects skips gracefully, no crash - pending_effects contains an entry for a fiber_id that was removed from tree - apply_effects returns original tree unchanged for that entry ## Acceptance criteria - mix test test/filament/use_effect_test.exs passes (8 tests) - mix compile --warnings-as-errors passes - Filament.LiveView.apply_effects/2 is pure (no assign/2 calls) and fully unit-testable - Effects run AFTER render, not during (verified by test 1 — effect agent not incremented during the render pass, only after apply_effects is called) - Cleanup functions run before re-fire and on unmount (tests 4 and 5) - No crashes when a fiber is unmounted between render and effect execution (test 8)
title: C4: Implement use_effect/2 — side effects with cleanup and lifecycle
